title: Switch the data import from multiple CSV files to a single SQLite database
body:
### Goal
Up to now the project has imported several separate CSV files. All of that data has now been bundled into one SQLite database file. Replace the CSV-based import with a database import so the whole project pulls from a single, consistent source.

### Tasks
- [ ] Work from a new branch and give it an appropriate name.
- [ ] Use the startercode below to write a script that downloads the SQLite file into a data folder. If the startercode does not work, log in to 'https://filesender.surf.nl/?s=transfer_detail&transfer_id=3731332', copy the download link and replace it in the startercode:
```r
# Download SQLite file from the provided URL
url <- "https://filesender.surf.nl/download.php??token=29803da2-2322-4844-aebf-7e0b95129957&files_ids=38390042"
destination_file <- "tiktok_students.sqlite"
# or whatever you want to name it

# Download the file
download.file(url, destfile = destination_file, mode = "wb")

cat("File downloaded successfully to:", destination_file, "\n")
```
- [ ] Replace the existing `read_csv()` calls with a database connection (use lecture code as a startingpoint).
- [ ] Remove the now-unused CSV import code and any CSV files that are no longer needed.
- [ ] Double check that downstream cleaning, analysis and visualization code still works with the tables loaded from the database (column names or types may differ slightly from the old CSVs).
- [ ] Update the Makefile so it depends on the SQLite file instead of the individual CSVs.

### Completion
- [ ] When everything runs correctly, create a Pull request on GitHub from your branch to your main branch (not to the main repository) and merge to main.

title: Create one regression analysis
body:
### Goal
Find one correlation in the data that seems interesting enough to look into further (this may be one you already came across during data inspection) and build a regression analysis around it.

### Tasks
- [ ] Pick one correlation from the data that you'd like to investigate further.
- [ ] Write a regression script, this startercode can be used:
```r
model <- lm(y ~ x, data = data)
```
- [ ] Expand the starter model with more variables and/or fixed effects, and inspect the model summary.
- [ ] Include the regression analysis output (e.g. `summary(model)` and plots) in the final summary.

### Completion
- [ ] When everything runs correctly, create a Pull request on GitHub from your branch to your main branch (not to the main repository) and merge to main.

title: Create a final analysis output
body:
### Goal
Bring everything together into one final, knitted report: the basic data inspection, the analyses/summaries, the regression analysis, and your conclusions, combined into a single PDF.

### Tasks
- [ ] Create one Quarto (or R Markdown) document that pulls together the basic data inspection, the summary analyses, and the regression analysis produced in the other issues.
- [ ] Add a short conclusions section that reflects on what the inspection and the regression showed (e.g. what the correlation you investigated means, and any caveats).
- [ ] Render/knit the document into a single PDF.
- [ ] Save the rendered PDF in an appropriate output folder, and make sure it can be reproduced by re-running the document.

### Completion
- [ ] When everything runs correctly, create a Pull request on GitHub from your branch to your main branch (not to the main repository) and merge to main.

title: Full automation
body:
### Goal
Make the whole project reproducible from a single command. Create one Makefile in the root of the repository that, when run, downloads the data, cleans it if necessary, runs the different summaries, runs the regression analysis, and combines all the outputs into the final PDF (or, if you want to take it further, into a dashboard).

### Tasks
- [ ] Create a single Makefile at the root of the repository that orchestrates the full pipeline end to end.
- [ ] Use proper Makefile targets and dependencies, so a step only reruns when its inputs have changed (not on every `make` call).
- [ ] (Optional, more advanced) In addition to a static PDF, turn the final output into an interactive dashboard (e.g. a Quarto dashboard or Shiny app) as the last step of the pipeline.

### Completion
- [ ] When everything runs correctly, create a Pull request on GitHub from your branch to your main branch (not to the main repository) and merge to main.
